findings.where: Page title (h1 'Best Hostels in Canggu'), checked against the whole page
findings.fault: The title promises a list of the best hostels, but the page lists none. The visitor only finds out at the very bottom, in the coming-soon block, after reading the whole guide. The first screen never says the page is a guide to the area rather than a ranking.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who arrived from search to pick a hostel. They feel baited when the page ends with no hostels, and that costs trust on their first visit to a brand whose product is trust.

findings.where: 'Good for' section, all twelve tag pills (First-time surfers to Sunsets), desktop and phone
findings.fault: Each tag is a filled, bordered capsule in a strong colour, which looks like a filter chip or a button. None of them can be tapped. On a hostel site the visitor expects tapping 'Budget' or 'Solo travellers' to filter hostels, and nothing happens.
findings.who_objects: A phone visitor who taps 'Budget' to narrow the choice and gets no response. They decide the page is broken.

findings.where: 'Good for' tag pills: their fills and borders
findings.fault: The tags use a rainbow of fills with clashing borders: pink, purple, magenta, red-coral, amber, two teals, and yellow with a red edge. Purple and pink are not brand colours. Amber is kept for rewards and coral for the one main button. Here the colours mean nothing, and the row turns into the loudest, most garish thing on the page.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose brand gives every colour one job and keeps coral off decoration. The visitor too: the eye jumps to a confetti strip that tells them nothing, and the page feels like a template rather than a hostel brand.

findings.fault: This one heading is set in italic turquoise and underlined, so it reads as a link, but it does nothing. It also breaks from its sibling headings 'Surf' and 'Good for', which are plain ink.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who clicks 'Vibe' expecting more about the party and nomad scene and gets nothing. A reader scanning the headings also wonders why this section looks special.

findings.where: Coming-soon block above the footer, desktop and phone
findings.fault: The notice sits on a saturated red panel, which reads as an error or a warning, not as friendly news that listings are on the way. The brand puts this kind of announcement on the dark ink ground. The text also fills only the left half of a full-width red box, leaving a large empty red area.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker, who thinks something has failed or been withdrawn. The founder, because red and coral as a ground is the Hostelworld-like warm field the brand rules out.

findings.where: Nav 'Destinations' and 'How we rank'; footer Privacy, Terms, How we rank, Report content
findings.fault: 'Destinations' points to a #destinations section that does not exist on this page. 'How we rank', 'Privacy', 'Terms' and 'Report content' all point back to this same page. Every way onward except the email link goes nowhere.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who wants to look at Uluwatu or Lombok next, or check how hostels will be ranked, or read the privacy terms. They hit dead ends, and on a pre-launch brand asking for trust that looks unfinished.

findings.where: End of the content, from 'What to look for' through the coming-soon block
findings.fault: The page offers no next step. A visitor who has decided Canggu suits them has nothing to do: they can't ask to be told when listings go live, there's no link to other destinations, and no route onward.
findings.who_objects: The planner, who leaves to book on an OTA. The founder, who loses the one visitor most likely to come back.

findings.where: Section headings: 'Surf', 'Vibe', 'Good for', 'WHAT TO LOOK FOR'
findings.fault: Four sibling sections use three different heading looks: plain Quicksand, italic underlined turquoise, and small letter-spaced capitals. 'What to look for' is the most useful part for choosing a hostel, yet it gets the smallest, quietest heading.
findings.who_objects: A visitor scanning for practical advice. They skim past the hostel-choosing tips because they look like a minor label.

findings.where: Body text throughout: the intro, Surf, Vibe and What to look for paragraphs, and the coming-soon block; worst on the phone in the coming-soon block
findings.fault: The text is justified, so narrow columns open uneven gaps between words. On the phone, 'MantaHostels   is   launching   across' is stretched across the line, and the rivers of space slow reading.
findings.who_objects: A phone reader on the move. Uneven spacing makes short lines harder to read and looks unpolished.

findings.fault: There is no hero: a small eyebrow and a title on plain sand, then a narrow text column pinned left with the right half of a 1440 px screen empty. Meanwhile the tag row and the red block run full width. The top of a destination page is meant to be the loud, beachy zone. This one reads sterile, with nothing to show what Canggu is like.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose brand names sterile as the enemy. The backpacker, who gets no sense of place and no reason to feel this brand knows Bali.

findings.fault: Twelve tags, including both Nightlife and Couples, and both Yoga and Scooter riders, say Canggu suits nearly everyone. That doesn't help the visitor judge whether it suits them, and the page never says who it does not suit.
findings.who_objects: A first-timer weighing Canggu against Ubud or the Gilis. They get no signal that separates it from anywhere else.

findings.fault: There's no sign the guide is current or who wrote it: no last-updated date and no author. The 'How we rank' explanation it would lean on goes nowhere.
findings.who_objects: A traveller relying on surf and area advice, which goes out of date. With no date they can't tell if the guide is fresh.
